title: Agent identity: whose permissions does an agent use?
summary: The identity mechanisms, control paths and Graph calls are supported by Microsoft documentation, including the corrected blueprint credentials and restricted sign-in query. One minor correction remains: acknowledge that Microsoft's agent-management pages give a different Conditional Access licensing requirement from its dedicated licensing section.

claims.claim: Control maker credential options is in Power Platform admin center under Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: In the environment's details page, select Settings on the top menu bar. Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section. ... Under Control maker credential options

claims.claim: An API for Control maker credential options was not found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" API; PowerShell API Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironment pac; REST Power Platform maker credentials. Opened configure-no-maker-authentication, pac copilot-studio, and Environment Management Settings update reference; none documents this setting's API.

claims.claim: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials is under Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an automation equivalent for the embedded-maker-credentials sharing setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" API PowerShell environment settings; "embedded maker credentials" "Power Platform API" "PowerShell". Opened both configuration pages, pac copilot-studio and Environment Management Settings update; no setting-specific call.

claims.claim: The maker configures connector credentials at Agents > agent > Tools > tool > Overview > Details > Additional details > Credentials to use.
claims.quote: Go to the connector tool Overview page. ... Under Details > Additional details > Credentials to use, select Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: No API equivalent is documented for the connector tool's Credentials to use choice.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio connector tool "Credentials to use" Dataverse API authentication; botcomponent authentication ConnectionReference. Opened advanced-connectors and pac copilot-studio; read tool-authentication and botcomponent reference excerpts; no equivalent call found.

claims.claim: Dataverse agent users are added through Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Agents > + Add agent.
claims.quote: In the command bar, select Settings. ... Expand Users + permissions, and then select Agents. ... Select + Add agent from the command bar. The Add agent pane appears.

claims.claim: No API for adding Dataverse agent users was found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "agent users" API add agent systemuser; Dataverse "agent users" "Web API"; Power Apps developer "agent user" Create. Opened create-users and agent-users; read SystemUser reference and Web API results; no agent-user provisioning call found.

claims.claim: Agent identities are accessible in Microsoft Entra admin center at Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Agents > Agent identities. ... Select any agent identity to view its details, including name, description, status, owners, sponsors, granted permissions, and sign-in logs.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph supports updating an agent identity with PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity.
claims.quote: Update the properties of an agentIdentity object. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/microsoft.graph.agentIdentity

claims.claim: Agent targeting is available under Assignments > Users, agents, or workload identities > Agents in Microsoft Entra Conditional Access.
claims.quote: Instead, to scope policies to agent users, under Assignments > Users, agents, or workload identities, select Agents, and then target all agent users or specific agent users.

claims.claim: The documented Graph POST to the beta identity/conditionalAccess/policies endpoint creates an all-agent-identity block policy in report-only state using a policy JSON body.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies ... "displayName": "Block all agent identities from accessing resources" ... "state": "enabledForReportingButNotEnforced"

claims.claim: Agent sign-ins are viewed at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs.

claims.claim: The documented agent-identity sign-in query is GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=signInEventTypes/any(t: t eq 'servicePrincipal') and agent/agentType eq 'AgentIdentity'

claims.claim: Environment Admin can configure maker credential options for a single environment.
claims.quote: Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator or Global Admin is required to configure maker credential options for environment groups.
claims.quote: Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups

claims.claim: The maker-credential control governs agents in the selected environment or environment group.
claims.quote: Choose whether end-user or maker credentials (or both) can be selected by makers for agents in an environment, or for all agents in all environments in an environment group.

claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials changes all tools for all agents in the affected environments immediately at runtime.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.claim: Administrators can permit maker-provided credentials, end-user credentials or both.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.claim: Both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled by default in the administrative control.
claims.quote: By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.claim: Environment-group maker credential settings override individual environment settings.
claims.quote: If an environment is part of a managed group where the policy is enabled, you can't individually disable it for one environment in that group - environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials setting is an environment-level control for Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: The Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting is an environment-level control for Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials sharing control is in preview.
claims.quote: Control sharing agents with embedded maker credentials (preview) ... [This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: All sharing allowed detects unsafe credential use and informs makers without blocking sharing.
claims.quote: All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn't block sharing.

claims.claim: Safe sharing enforced blocks applicable publishing or sharing paths for unsafe agents.
claims.quote: Safe sharing enforced | Copilot Studio blocks applicable publish or share paths when an agent is unsafe for sharing.

claims.claim: Enabling the embedded-credentials control does not retroactively unshare existing agents.
claims.quote: The control doesn't retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.

claims.claim: Enabling the embedded-credentials control does not retroactively disable existing agents.
claims.quote: The control doesn't retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.

claims.claim: The embedded-credentials control enforces at sharing and publishing rather than blocking a running agent.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn't block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: Using maker-provided credentials for connector tools requires an authenticated channel.
claims.quote: To have your agent use the maker's credentials, follow these steps: ... Configure your agent to use an authenticated channel.

claims.claim: The default credential option for connectors and flows is End user credentials.
claims.quote: The default option for connectors and flows is End user credentials, and the security scan provides a warning if the maker changes it to Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: Adding Dataverse agent users is a preview feature.
claims.quote: Create an agent user (preview) ... This is a preview feature.

claims.claim: An administrator chooses an agent user and adds it to the selected environment.
claims.quote: Choose the agent user from the search list, and then select Add to add the agent.

claims.claim: The administrator assigns the added Dataverse agent a security role.
claims.quote: On the Manage security roles page, select a security role for your agent. ... Select Save to apply the changes.

claims.claim: Agent ID Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator can manage agent identities.
claims.quote: Manage agent identities | Agent ID Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator

claims.claim: Agent identity owners can manage their own agents without those administrator roles.
claims.quote: Agent identity owners can manage their own agents without these roles.

claims.claim: The agentIdentity update API lists AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All as a least-privileged permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | AgentIdentity.EnableDisable.All | AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: Configuring Conditional Access policies requires Conditional Access Administrator.
claims.quote: Configure Conditional Access policies | Conditional Access Administrator

claims.claim: Viewing agent sign-in logs requires at least Reports Reader.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Reports Reader.

claims.claim: Agent type is an available sign-in log filter.
claims.quote: Agent type: Choose from Agent ID user, Agent Identity, Agent Identity Blueprint or Not Agentic

claims.claim: Is Agent is an available sign-in log filter.
claims.quote: Is Agent: Choose from No or Yes

claims.claim: The printed Graph query returns only service-principal sign-in events for AgentIdentity, not every agent-related sign-in type.
claims.quote: This request is limited to service principal sign-in events where the agent type is AgentIdentity. It doesn't retrieve all agent-related sign-in types.

claims.claim: With end-user credentials, the user signs into the connected service and the action runs as that user.
claims.quote: Once the user signs in with their own account for the required service, the agent proceeds with the action using the user's credentials. ... The action runs under the end-user's identity.

claims.claim: An end-user-authenticated action cannot perform an operation for which the user lacks permission.
claims.quote: If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: Maker-provided connections authenticate with the maker's credentials instead of the interacting user's credentials.
claims.quote: When someone uses the agent, the agent uses the maker's credentials, not the end user's credentials, to authenticate with connected services.

claims.claim: Maker-provided credentials can expose data or actions unavailable to the end user.
claims.quote: Using maker credentials could lead to oversharing of data or capabilities - for example, an end user might retrieve information or perform actions that only the maker's account is permitted to do.

claims.claim: Microsoft names service principals, API keys and managed identities as examples of approved system identities.
claims.quote: Agents that use an approved system identity, such as a service principal, API key, or managed identity, can be published when the associated connection supports the scenario.

claims.claim: Service-account access is governed by the permissions granted to that account.
claims.quote: When you create service accounts for automated use, they're granted permissions to access resources in Azure and Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent can have its own identity in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: An account used by an AI agent is referred to as an agent identity.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Entra agent-identity access depends on granted permissions and applicable policies.
claims.quote: If the required controls are satisfied, access is granted. ... If the required controls are not satisfied, access is denied.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs capture agent activity.
claims.quote: Agent identity activities are captured in Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs

claims.claim: The credentials choice is configured on the individual connector tool.
claims.quote: Go to the connector tool Overview page. ... Under Details > Additional details > Credentials to use, select Maker-provided credentials.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent identity is a special service principal in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: An agent identity is a special service principal in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Credentials are configured on the blueprint rather than the agent identity.
claims.quote: Credentials are configured on the blueprint, not the agent identity.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: In multi-instance mode the blueprint impersonates its child agent identities.
claims.quote: In multi-instance mode, the blueprint impersonates its child agent identities.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: In single-instance mode the Agent ID requests tokens directly.
claims.quote: In single-instance mode, the blueprint and Agent ID share an OAuth client ID, and the Agent ID requests tokens directly.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio automatically provisions Entra Agent IDs for new agents.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically provisions Entra Agent IDs for new agents. The timing of Entra Agent ID provisioning depends on the harness that powers the agent.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Agents created before the May 2026 implementation continue using traditional app registrations.
claims.quote: Existing agents that you created before Entra Agent ID was implemented in May 2026 continue using traditional app registrations.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Nobody in the tenant, including administrators, can generate tokens using a Copilot Studio Entra agent identity.
claims.quote: No one in your tenant - including tenant administrators - can generate tokens by using the agent identity. Microsoft fully controls the blueprint and authentication mechanism.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent's user account is optional.
claims.quote: Agent's user account (optional).

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: An agent's user account is a separate object with an id different from the agent identity.
claims.quote: This second account is a user account in the Microsoft Entra tenant that is decorated as an AI agent. It has a different id than the agent identity

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: The agent identity and its agent user account have a one-to-one relationship.
claims.quote: a 1:1 relationship is always established between an agent identity and its agent's user account.

claims.where: What it is: Entra agent identity
claims.claim: Agent user accounts support systems that require Microsoft Entra user-account authentication.
claims.quote: Some agents need access to systems that strictly require a Microsoft Entra user account be used for authentication. In these cases, an agent can be given a second account, called an agent's user account.

claims.claim: Federated connectors in Microsoft 365 Copilot access data with the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.claim: Federated connector tools that write data initially require the user's explicit approval.
claims.quote: Tools that create, update, or delete data initially require the user's explicit approval.

claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses further approval prompts for the tool during that conversation.
claims.quote: Allow for conversation | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.claim: Always allow can suppress subsequent approval prompts for that tool.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.claim: Allow for conversation and Always allow permissions apply to an individual tool.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector.

claims.claim: In preview, a published agent with triggers can be shared for users to run with their own credentials.
claims.quote: Share an autonomous agent for users to run (preview) ... You can share a published agent that has triggers with users who need to run the agent by using their own credentials.

claims.claim: Sharing that autonomous agent requires configuring its triggers and tools for user authentication first.
claims.quote: Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio runs a security scan automatically before publishing.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically runs a security scan and warns makers before publishing.

claims.claim: The security scan warns makers when they select maker-provided credentials for connectors and flows.
claims.quote: the security scan provides a warning if the maker changes it to Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: There is no documented setting for the automatic maker security scan.
claims.quote: Searched: "security scan" "Copilot Studio" disable configuration. Opened security-scan; read security-and-governance search excerpts. These describe automatic maker warnings, not a configurable scan setting; no setting found.

claims.claim: The maker-credential setting's Copilot Studio page names no licence or meter for the setting.
claims.quote: Prerequisites ... Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: The embedded-credential setting's Copilot Studio page names no licence or meter for the setting.
claims.quote: To configure Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials, you need permission to manage settings for the target Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 is one qualifying licence plan for Conditional Access for agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access for agents requires one of the following license plans: ... Microsoft 365 E7, which includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite.
claims.fix: After the Conditional Access licensing bullet, add: "Microsoft's agent-management and disable-agent-identities pages instead state that Conditional Access requires Entra ID P1; this differs from the dedicated Conditional Access for agents licensing section." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/manage-agent-identities-admin and https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/agent-id/disable-agent-identities, both already in sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E7, which includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite.

claims.claim: Microsoft Agent 365 paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3 is the other documented qualifying plan.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 license paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.

claims.claim: ID Protection for agents requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 during preview.
claims.quote: ID Protection for agents requires a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license during preview.

claims.claim: Each Copilot Studio Entra Agent ID counts as a directory object against the tenant resource quota.
claims.quote: Every Microsoft Entra Agent ID that Copilot Studio creates is a directory object in your tenant and counts against your tenant's resource quota in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: The normal default tenant resource quota is 50,000 directory objects.
claims.quote: Tenant resource quota: 50,000 directory objects by default, or 300,000 if your tenant has a verified domain.

claims.claim: A verified domain normally raises the tenant resource quota to 300,000 directory objects.
claims.quote: Tenant resource quota: 50,000 directory objects by default, or 300,000 if your tenant has a verified domain.

claims.claim: Self-service-signup tenants remain at 50,000 directory objects even after domain verification.
claims.quote: Tenants created through self-service signup remain at 50,000 even after a domain is verified.

claims.claim: Each end user's autonomous-agent usage is totalled and billed through the hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcing end-user credentials
claims.claim: Blocking maker credentials causes scheduled, autonomous-event and background agents without a live user sign-in to fail.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials. All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Conditional Access channel limitation
claims.claim: Copilot Studio connector scope visibility in Entra applies to all agents regardless of channel.
claims.quote: Scope visibility in Microsoft Entra ID applies to all agents, regardless of channel.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Risks and limits; Open questions
claims.claim: Conditional Access enforcement on Copilot Studio agent identities for connector calls currently applies only in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: Scope enforcement at runtime — including Microsoft Entra Conditional Access on the agent identity — currently applies only when the agent runs in Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: Resource access through an API key bypasses Entra authentication and token issuance, so Conditional Access does not apply to it.
claims.quote: if an agent accesses resources using an API key, it bypasses the Microsoft Entra ID authentication and token issuance pipeline entirely and Conditional Access policies won't apply to them.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Agent user accounts
claims.claim: A Conditional Access policy targeting an agent identity does not apply to the agent's user account.
claims.quote: A policy that targets an agent identity doesn't apply to the agent's user account, and a policy that targets the agent's user account doesn't apply to the agent identity.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Agent user accounts
claims.claim: Targeting agent identities through a blueprint likewise does not cover their agent user accounts.
claims.quote: A Conditional Access policy targeting agent identities using agent identity blueprint covers only the agent identity, not the agent's user account.

claims.claim: The connector-scope behaviour applies to first-party and certified Power Platform connectors.
claims.quote: Today, this behavior applies to first-party and certified Power Platform connectors

claims.claim: Custom connectors, MCP servers and REST API tools do not add API permissions to the Entra Agent ID.
claims.quote: custom connectors, MCP servers, and REST API tools added to agents don't add API permissions to the Entra Agent ID.

claims.claim: Reaching the tenant's Entra quota can prevent identity provisioning and cause agent creation to fail.
claims.quote: If the tenant reaches its quota at that time, Copilot Studio can't create the Microsoft Entra Agent ID and the agent fails to be created.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Disabling all agent identities
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that globally disabling agent identities can make existing agents fail.
claims.quote: Existing agents running in your organization might begin to fail.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Disabling all agent identities
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that globally disabling agent identities can push teams toward less transparent application or service-principal identities.
claims.quote: Globally disabling agent identities can cause existing agents to fail, degrade Microsoft product experiences, and push teams to use less transparent application or service principal identities.

claims.claim: The second cited embedded-credentials Learn page documents a different route through Security > Threat detection, as the page explicitly acknowledges.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Security, and then select Threat detection. ... Select Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials. A panel opens.

claims.claim: The maker-credential control pages do not explain how audit records attribute the interacting user when maker credentials are used.
claims.quote: Searched: "maker-provided credentials" "audit" interacting user. Opened configure-no-maker-authentication, configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and the Power Platform sharing-control page; none specifies interacting-user audit attribution.
